# Review standards

What blocks a merge in an independent review of this repository. This file
holds judgement rules only; every mechanical rule runs in `scripts/check.sh`.
Each rule names the incident that taught it
([EPG-DEC-0001](decisions/EPG-DEC-0001-reconcile-entire-and-dagger.md) set this
file up).

- None recorded yet. A rule lands here only after a reviewer actually made the
  finding, with the pull request that carried it.

# Decision records

| Record | Title | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [EPG-DEC-0001](EPG-DEC-0001-reconcile-entire-and-dagger.md) | Reconcile Entire and Dagger with the way-of-working guardrails | Decided |

One record per decision, with context, the decision and the owner's recorded
words, alternatives, evidence, and status. `scripts/check.sh` compares each
record's `Status` field with this table; a change to one updates the other in
the same pull request.

# EPG-DEC-0001 — Reconcile Entire and Dagger with the way-of-working guardrails

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Record ID | EPG-DEC-0001 |
| Status | Decided |
| Date | 2026-11-08 |
| Decided by | Hamid Adesokan (owner) |

## Context

The repository runs Entire (session check-pointing, trails) and Dagger
(container checks in `.dagger`) beside the `way-of-working` guardrails. Entire
had installed its Git hooks into `.git/hooks`, so no tracked pre-push hook ran
the check script, which is what the guardrails require before every push. The
guardrails say an existing or shared hook setup is reported and wired by the
owner's decision, not overwritten.

## Recommendation presented

The recommendation the owner answered, from the session message of 2026-11-08
(condensed; the original message carried the same options in full): keep the
division of labor of GitHub pull request as the review and merge surface,
Entire trails as the project-level record with findings instead of comments,
and Dagger as the container check runner; and wire the checks into the
repository by tracking delegating hooks in `scripts/hooks`, pointing
`core.hooksPath` there through `scripts/bootstrap.sh`, with each hook
delegating to Entire when its CLI is installed and degrading silently when it
is not — so the tracked-hook model of way-of-working keeps working in any
repository, Entire or not.

## Decision

The owner's words, quoted verbatim from the 2026-11-08 session message
(no Markdown stripped, typos kept):

"let us address all of this. Please do not modify way of working dramatically. It needs to keep working where there is no entire and dagger. but must work together when they are all present . Also adress the small items take insipration from enteprise performance model repo AGENTS.md

have whatever we do be reivewed by independent review as required by way of working"

## What this settles and what stays open

- Settled: the reconciliation runs in this repository, on the owner's words,
  with the way-of-working skill left unchanged.
- Settled: every change from this work goes through the independent review the
  owner restated ("have whatever we do be reivewed...").
- Proposed, pending the owner's confirmation on the pull request: the hook
  wiring detail — tracked delegating hooks in `scripts/hooks` plus
  `core.hooksPath` — rather than wrapping the untracked `.git/hooks/pre-push`
  in place. The owner's message names the direction (way-of-working keeps
  working without Entire and Dagger) but not this detail. Either choice
  satisfies what the owner said; `scripts/hooks` was chosen because it is
  tracked and survives a fresh clone.

## Alternatives considered

- Wrapping `entire`'s hooks in `.git/hooks` in place: not tracked, lost on a
  fresh clone, and overwritten by an Entire CLI update or reinstall.
- Leaving hook checks out and relying on Dagger CI alone: breaks the
  check-before-every-push rule wherever Dagger or CI is absent, and this
  repository currently has no GitHub workflow running Dagger.

## Evidence

- `git config core.hooksPath` printed nothing; `.git/hooks` held Entire's
  five hooks (`prepare-commit-msg`, `commit-msg`, `post-commit`, `post-rewrite`,
  `pre-push`), each delegating to `entire hooks git <name>`.
- `entire agent-help` on 2026-11-08: `pre-push` pushes session logs alongside
  the user's push; checkpoints sync on commit; trails span repositories.
- `entire doctor` on 2026-11-08 reported hooks OK and finalized 2 exited
  sessions; it re-ran clean after the wiring.
- The Dagger module `.dagger/modules/people-graph-ci` ran three checks
  (markdown structure, link targets, checker tests) in containers, mounted
  from the repository's Markdown include set.

#!/bin/sh
# Wire this repository's tracked hooks for the first time (a fresh clone runs
# this once; see AGENTS.md, "Before every push").
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

chmod +x scripts/check.sh scripts/hooks/*
git config core.hooksPath scripts/hooks

echo "core.hooksPath -> $(git config core.hooksPath)"
echo "Hooks:" "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/$(git config core.hooksPath)"

#!/bin/sh
# The one check script: every mechanical gate, run locally, by the pre-push
# hook (scripts/hooks/pre-push) and by CI (.github/workflows/check.yml).
#
# Plain run: the check tools, directly, with the local Node. Works in any
# clone and needs neither Entire nor Dagger.
# `--with-dagger`: additionally runs the same three checks in the containers
# of .dagger (module people-graph-ci) when the dagger CLI is on PATH.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

if [ "${1:-}" = "--with-dagger" ]; then
  if command -v dagger >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dagger check
  else
    echo "check: --with-dagger set but the dagger CLI is not on PATH; running local checks only." >&2
  fi
fi

# The checks read the tree; none may write it. Snapshot, run, compare.
tree_before=$(git status --porcelain)

(
  cd ci
  if [ ! -d node_modules ] \
    || [ package.json -nt node_modules ] \
    || [ package-lock.json -nt node_modules ]; then
    npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
  fi
)

# 1. The check tool's own tests.
(cd ci && npm test)

# 2. Markdown structure over the tracked set — the same population the Dagger
# module mounts (see .dagger/modules/people-graph-ci/src/index.ts).
git ls-files '*.md' | tr '\n' '\0' | xargs -0 \
  ci/node_modules/.bin/markdownlint-cli2 --config ci/markdownlint-cli2.jsonc

# 3. Local link and image targets. The checker skips node_modules and
# dot-directories, so scanning the repository root matches the Dagger mount.
node ci/check-links.mjs .

# 4. Each decision record's Status agrees with docs/decisions/INDEX.md.
status_failures=0
for record in docs/decisions/EPG-DEC-*.md; do
  [ -e "$record" ] || break
  record_status=$(awk -F' *\\| *' '/^\| Status \|/ {print $3; exit}' "$record")
  record_id=$(basename "$record" | cut -d- -f1-3)
  index_status=$(awk -F' *\\| *' -v id="$record_id" \
    '$0 ~ "\\| \\["id"\\] \\(" {print $4; exit}' docs/decisions/INDEX.md)
  if [ "$record_status" != "$index_status" ]; then
    echo "check: $record Status '$record_status' disagrees with docs/decisions/INDEX.md '$index_status'" >&2
    status_failures=1
  fi
done
[ "$status_failures" -eq 0 ]

tree_after=$(git status --porcelain)
if [ "$tree_before" != "$tree_after" ]; then
  echo "check: the checks modified the working tree" >&2
  diff -u <(printf '%s\n' "$tree_before") <(printf '%s\n' "$tree_after") >&2 || true
  exit 1
fi

echo "check: all checks passed."

#!/bin/sh
# Tracked pre-push hook. core.hooksPath -> scripts/hooks; install with
# scripts/bootstrap.sh. See AGENTS.md, "Before every push".
#
# Runs the check script on any push that sends commits, then hands the push to
# Entire's session-log sync when the Entire CLI is installed. A push whose
# every ref is a deletion sends no commits and skips the checks.
#
# Entire installs its original of this hook into .git/hooks, which
# core.hooksPath hides, so this tracked delegation keeps both flows working.
# Keep the Entire arguments in step with Entire's installed hook.
input=$(cat)
send_commits=$(printf '%s\n' "$input" | awk '$2 !~ /^0+$/ {found=1} END {print found+0}')
if [ "$send_commits" -eq 1 ]; then
  "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/scripts/check.sh"
fi

if printf '%s' "$input" | if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then entire hooks git pre-push "$1"; else :; fi; then
  :
fi

#!/bin/sh
# Tracked delegation to Entire's commit-msg hook (strips the Entire-Checkpoint
# trailer when the commit has no user content, allowing an aborted empty
# commit). Entire installs its original into .git/hooks, which the
# core.hooksPath set by scripts/bootstrap.sh hides; this copy keeps both flows
# working. Keep the arguments in step with Entire's installed hook.
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then entire hooks git commit-msg "$1" || true; else printf '%s\n' '[entire] Entire CLI is enabled but not installed or not on PATH. Skipping Entire Git hook; continuing. Installation guide: https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation#installation-methods' >&2 || :; fi

#!/bin/sh
# Tracked delegation to Entire's prepare-commit-msg hook (appends the
# Entire-Checkpoint trailer). Entire installs its original into .git/hooks,
# which the core.hooksPath set by scripts/bootstrap.sh hides; this copy keeps
# both flows working. Keep the arguments in step with Entire's installed hook.
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || true; else :; fi

#!/bin/sh
# Tracked delegation to Entire's post-commit hook (condenses session data when
# the commit carries the Entire-Checkpoint trailer). Entire installs its
# original into .git/hooks, which the core.hooksPath set by
# scripts/bootstrap.sh hides; this copy keeps both flows working. Keep the
# arguments in step with Entire's installed hook.
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then entire hooks git post-commit 2>/dev/null || true; else :; fi

#!/bin/sh
# Tracked delegation to Entire's post-rewrite hook (remaps session linkage
# after amend, rebase, or other history rewrites). Entire installs its
# original into .git/hooks, which the core.hooksPath set by
# scripts/bootstrap.sh hides; this copy keeps both flows working. Keep the
# arguments in step with Entire's installed hook.
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then entire hooks git post-rewrite "$1" 2>/dev/null || true; else :; fi

# Agent instructions — enterprise-people-graph

Shared instructions for coding agents working in this repo (Claude Code reads
this file through `CLAUDE.md`; Codex and Cursor read it directly). Start at
[LIONG-README](LIONG_Design_Document_Package/README.md) for orientation, at
[LIONG-REG-001](LIONG_Design_Document_Package/LIONG-REG-001_Assumptions_Decisions_and_Open_Questions.md)
for requirement authority and open questions, and at
[the decision record index](docs/decisions/INDEX.md) for process decisions.

## Skills every agent loads

- **Writing for a person:** load the `clear-writing` skill first and follow it.
  That covers every reply, status update, doc, README, commit message, PR
  description, and any text the user asks to edit. Subagents load it too.
- **Changing the repo:** load the `way-of-working` skill first and follow it.
  Where this file sets its own rule, this file wins
  ([EPG-DEC-0001](docs/decisions/EPG-DEC-0001-reconcile-entire-and-dagger.md)
  records the owner's choice).

## Before every push

1. **`scripts/check.sh` passes.** It runs the check tool's tests, Markdown
   structure over the tracked Markdown, local link checks, and the
   decision-record index comparison. CI
   ([`.github/workflows/check.yml`](.github/workflows/check.yml)) and the
   pre-push hook run it too. With the `dagger` CLI installed,
   `scripts/check.sh --with-dagger` additionally runs the container checks of
   the Dagger module (`.dagger`); a plain run is identical without them.
2. **The hooks are wired.** A fresh clone runs `./scripts/bootstrap.sh` once;
   it sets `core.hooksPath` to `scripts/hooks`. The hook files delegate to
   Entire, so Entire's checkpoints and session-log sync keep working, and
   degrade silently when Entire is not installed. On a machine where Entire
   re-manages `.git/hooks`, that remains Entire's own state; this repo's hook
   entry point stays `scripts/hooks`.
3. **The independent review runs on the committed diff** before the pull
   request opens, per the `way-of-working` skill's review order. The findings
   are fixed or answered before the push.

## Working rules

- **Every change goes through a pull request.** One concern per PR. A reviewer
  merges or holds; address holds on the same branch.
- **Nothing is Decided or Approved without the owner's recorded words**, quoted
  in a [decision record](docs/decisions/INDEX.md). Decision records live in
  `docs/decisions/`; one record per decision, with its index row kept in step.
  What blocks a merge in review is in
  [REVIEW_STANDARDS.md](docs/REVIEW_STANDARDS.md).

## Entire and Dagger (EPG-DEC-0001)

- The **GitHub pull request** is the code-review and merge surface. Entire
  trails hold project-level intent across repositories: keep the trail
  description current after work, post project-level findings with
  `entire trail finding` (never as comments), and link the trail URL in the PR
  when one exists. Merging code goes through the reviewed PR, not
  `entire trail merge`.
- **Checkpoints are automatic.** The commit hooks capture the AI session; do
  not create manual checkpoints unless the owner asks.
- **Dagger** (`.dagger`, module `people-graph-ci`) runs the checks in
  containers. Its Markdown set and `scripts/check.sh`'s must stay the same
  population; a change to one is a change to the other in the same PR.
- **Everything degrades.** Without Entire, the hooks run their non-Entire
  parts and print Entire's fallback note. Without Dagger, `check.sh` runs the
  same checks through the local Node. Without CI, the pre-push hook is still
  the gate.

## Agent skills

GitHub Issues are the issue tracker through the `gh` CLI; PR bodies are not a
triage surface.

#!/bin/bash
# The one check script: every mechanical gate, run locally, by the pre-push
# hook (scripts/hooks/pre-push) and by CI (.github/workflows/check.yml).
#
# Plain run: the check tools, directly, with the local Node. Works in any
# clone and needs neither Entire nor Dagger.
# `--with-dagger`: additionally runs the same checks in the containers of
# .dagger (module people-graph-ci) when the dagger CLI is on PATH. Like every
# step between the two snapshot points, a Dagger-side tree change fails the
# check.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

# The checks read the repository; none of them may change it. The guard
# hashes every file system entry's contents, type, mode and symlink target,
# plus the index blobs and git's status view, before and after
# (scripts/tree-guard.mjs; its comment names the excluded paths and why).
guard_state=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-tree-guard.XXXXXX")
list_state=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-md-files.XXXXXX")
md_list=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-md-existing.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "$guard_state" "$list_state" "$md_list"' EXIT
node scripts/tree-guard.mjs snapshot "$guard_state"

if [ "${1:-}" = "--with-dagger" ]; then
  if command -v dagger >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    dagger check
  else
    echo "check: --with-dagger set but the dagger CLI is not on PATH; running local checks only." >&2
  fi
fi

# ci dependencies: install when the folder is missing or older than the
# manifests. Installs outside the guarded population (see tree-guard).
(
  cd ci
  if [ ! -d node_modules ] \
    || [ package.json -nt node_modules ] \
    || [ package-lock.json -nt node_modules ]; then
    npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
  fi
)

# 1. The check tools' own tests (link checker, tree guard, decision guard).
(cd ci && npm test)

# 2. Markdown structure over the tracked Markdown. The population is every
# tracked *.md, and each file must live inside one of the Dagger mount's
# roots (asserted here), so the local and container checks cannot silently
# diverge (mount roots: .dagger/modules/people-graph-ci/src/index.ts).
git ls-files -z -- '*.md' > "$list_state"
if [ ! -s "$list_state" ]; then
  echo "check: no tracked Markdown files; refusing to run an empty check" >&2
  exit 1
fi
status=0
while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
  if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
    echo "check: tracked Markdown missing on disk: $file" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  case "$file" in
    */*) case "$file" in
           .github/*|docs/*|guideline_to_map_ontology_to_LPG/*|LIONG_Design_Document_Package/*) ;;
           *) echo "check: tracked Markdown outside the checked population: $file — add its root to .dagger/modules/people-graph-ci/src/index.ts and this case" >&2
              status=1 ;;
         esac ;;
  esac
  printf '%s\0' "$file" >> "$md_list"
done < "$list_state"
[ "$status" -eq 0 ]
bash scripts/lint-md.sh < "$md_list"

# 3. Local link and image targets. The checker follows symlinks, skips
# node_modules and tool dot-directories (except .github), and scans the
# repository root, so a local scan matches the Dagger mount.
node ci/check-links.mjs .

# 4. Each decision record's Status agrees with docs/decisions/INDEX.md,
# checked fail-closed (scripts/check-decisions.mjs).
node scripts/check-decisions.mjs docs/decisions

# 5. The behavioral harness for the gate itself.
bash scripts/gates.test.sh

# The tree must be exactly as the snapshot left it: contents, entry types,
# modes, symlink targets, index blobs, and git's status view.
node scripts/tree-guard.mjs verify "$guard_state"

echo "check: all checks passed."

# Agent instructions — enterprise-people-graph

Shared instructions for coding agents working in this repo (Claude Code loads
this file through [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md); Codex and Cursor read it directly).
Start at [LIONG-README](LIONG_Design_Document_Package/README.md) for
orientation, at
[LIONG-REG-001](LIONG_Design_Document_Package/LIONG-REG-001_Assumptions_Decisions_and_Open_Questions.md)
for requirement authority and open questions, and at
[the decision record index](docs/decisions/INDEX.md) for process decisions.

## Skills every agent loads

- **Writing for a person:** before writing anything a person will read, load
  the `clear-writing` skill and follow it — every reply, status update, doc,
  README, commit message, PR description, and any text the user asks to edit.
  Subagents load it too.
- **Changing the repo:** before changing anything, load the `way-of-working`
  skill and follow it. It owns the pull-request flow, the checks before every
  push, the independent review, watching open PRs, and the decision rules;
  this file points rather than restates. Where this file sets its own rule,
  this file wins; the hook wiring below is its one project-specific decision
  ([EPG-DEC-0001](docs/decisions/EPG-DEC-0001-reconcile-entire-and-dagger.md)).

## Before every push

1. **`scripts/check.sh` passes.** It runs the check tools' tests, lints the
   tracked Markdown, checks local link targets, verifies the decision-record
   index, runs the gate harness, and proves the run left the tree unchanged.
   CI ([`.github/workflows/check.yml`](.github/workflows/check.yml)) and the
   pre-push hook run the same script. With the `dagger` CLI installed,
   `scripts/check.sh --with-dagger` additionally runs the container checks of
   the Dagger module; a plain run is the same checks without the containers.
2. **The hooks are wired.** A fresh clone runs `./scripts/bootstrap.sh` once;
   it sets `core.hooksPath` to `scripts/hooks`. Each hook chains the check
   script ahead of a verbatim copy of Entire's hook, so Entire's checkpoints
   and session-log sync keep working. With Entire absent, `commit-msg` prints
   Entire's fallback note and the other four hooks run their non-Entire parts
   silently. **Status:** the tracked hook wiring is Proposed per
   [EPG-DEC-0001](docs/decisions/EPG-DEC-0001-reconcile-entire-and-dagger.md)
   until the pull request that adds it merges; confirm and update this file
   at merge, not before.
3. **The independent review runs on the committed diff** before the pull
   request opens, in the `way-of-working` skill's reviewer order.

## Entire and Dagger (EPG-DEC-0001)

- The **GitHub pull request** is the code-review and merge surface. Entire
  trails hold project-level intent across repositories: keep a trail's
  description current, post project-level findings with
  `entire trail finding` (never as comments), link the trail in the PR body,
  and merge code through the reviewed PR, not `entire trail merge`.
- **Checkpoints are automatic.** The commit hooks capture the AI session; do
  not create manual checkpoints unless the owner asks.
- **Dagger** (`.dagger`, module `people-graph-ci`) runs the checks in
  containers. Its mount roots and the tracked-Markdown population are one
  population: `check.sh` fails on a tracked Markdown file outside the roots
  that `src/index.ts` mounts, so the two sides cannot silently diverge.
- **Degradation.** Without Entire, the hooks run their non-Entire parts.
  Without Dagger, `check.sh` runs the same checks through the local Node; the
  container gate is `--with-dagger`. Without CI, the pre-push hook is still
  the gate.

## Agent skills

GitHub Issues are the issue tracker through the `gh` CLI; PR bodies are not a
triage surface.

Claude Code: read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and follow it as this repository's
agent instructions.

# EPG-DEC-0001 — Reconcile Entire and Dagger with the way-of-working guardrails

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Record ID | EPG-DEC-0001 |
| Status | Decided |
| Date | 2026-11-08 |
| Decided by | Hamid Adesokan (owner) |
| Amended | 2026-11-08 (Kimi reviewer flags; see the amendment below) |

## Context

The repository runs Entire (session check-pointing, trails) and Dagger
(container checks in `.dagger`) beside the `way-of-working` guardrails. Entire
had installed its Git hooks into `.git/hooks`, so no tracked pre-push hook ran
the check script, which is what the guardrails require before every push. The
guardrails say an existing or shared hook setup is reported and wired by the
owner's decision, not overwritten.

## Recommendation presented

The recommendation the owner answered, quoted verbatim from the agent's
session message of 2026-11-08 (Markdown kept, nothing shortened):

"## Division of labor (one source of truth per rule)

- **GitHub PR:** code review and merge. Way-of-working rule 2 stays here.
- **Entire trail:** project-level record across repos and branches. Keep the trail description current with `entire trail update`, post project-level findings with `entire trail finding`. The trail description should point to the repo's decision records, not restate them.
- **Dagger:** runs the check script in CI.

## The real clash: pre-push

`core.hooksPath` is unset and Entire has installed its own hooks directly in `.git/hooks`: `prepare-commit-msg`, `commit-msg`, `post-commit`, `post-rewrite`, and `pre-push`. Entire's `pre-push` only pushes session logs. Way-of-working session-start step 3 expects a tracked pre-push hook that runs one check script, and its own rule says: report a shared or existing hook setup and ask, rather than overwrite it.

Two options for you to decide:

1. **Wrap the hook (my recommendation).** `.git/hooks/pre-push` runs the check script first, then `entire hooks git pre-push`. The check script lives in the repo (Dagger CI calls the same one), and the hook delegates to Entire last. Risk to verify: an Entire CLI update or reinstall may rewrite the hook, so the wrapper needs re-applying — test before committing to it.
2. **Track a `.githooks/` directory and set `core.hooksPath`.** Each hook delegates to Entire, and pre-push runs the check script plus `entire hooks git pre-push`. Cleaner because everything is tracked, but it changes where Entire's hooks live, and I don't know yet whether Entire installs into a custom `hooksPath`."

## Decision

The owner's words, quoted verbatim from the 2026-11-08 session message
(two messages, joined in the order sent; no Markdown stripped, typos kept):

"let us address all of this. Please do not modify way of working dramatically. It needs to keep working where there is no entire and dagger. but must work together when they are all present . Also adress the small items take insipration from enteprise performance model repo AGENTS.md

have whatever we do be reivewed by independent review as required by way of working"

## What this settles and what stays open

- Settled by the owner's words: the reconciliation runs in this repository;
  the way-of-working skill is not modified dramatically and keeps working in
  repositories with neither Entire nor Dagger; every change goes through the
  independent review the owner restated; the process file takes its shape
  from the Enterprise Performance Model repository's `AGENTS.md`.
- Proposed, pending the owner's confirmation on the pull request: the hook
  wiring detail — tracked delegating hooks in `scripts/hooks` plus
  `core.hooksPath` — rather than wrapping the untracked `.git/hooks/pre-push`
  in place. The owner's message names the direction (way-of-working keeps
  working without Entire and Dagger) but not this detail. Either option
  above satisfies what the owner said; option 2's shape (as `scripts/hooks`)
  was chosen because it is tracked and survives a fresh clone. When the pull
  request merges with the owner's confirmation, remove the Proposed marker
  from `AGENTS.md` and here.

## Alternatives considered

- Wrapping `entire`'s hooks in `.git/hooks` in place (option 1 of the
  recommendation): not tracked, lost on a fresh clone, and overwritten by an
  Entire CLI update or reinstall.
- Leaving hook checks out and relying on Dagger CI alone: breaks the
  check-before-every-push rule wherever Dagger or CI is absent, and this
  repository currently has no GitHub workflow running Dagger.

## Evidence

- `git config core.hooksPath` printed nothing; `.git/hooks` held Entire's
  five hooks (`prepare-commit-msg`, `commit-msg`, `post-commit`, `post-rewrite`,
  `pre-push`), each delegating to `entire hooks git <name>`.
- `entire agent-help` on 2026-11-08: `pre-push` pushes session logs alongside
  the user's push; checkpoints sync on commit; trails span repositories.
- `entire doctor` on 2026-11-08 reported hooks OK and finalized 2 exited
  sessions; it re-ran clean after the wiring.
- The Dagger module `.dagger/modules/people-graph-ci` ran three checks
  (markdown structure, link targets, checker tests) in containers, mounted
  from the repository's Markdown include set.

## Amendment 2026-11-08 — Kimi reviewer flags

Mid-review, the owner said (quoted verbatim, from the 2026-11-08 session
message):

"kimi is asking for approval. can we open it to give it auto approval next time"

The agent changed the way-of-working review scripts' Kimi flags from `-y`
(Ask When Needed, whose read-approval prompts had blocked the running
review) to `--auto` (Never Ask), in `herdr-review.sh`, `hc-review.sh`,
`rex-review.sh` and their three test suites, and changed the matching line in
`references/before-push.md`. These files live in the `personal-agent-skills`
repository, not in this one; those edits are pending that repository's own
review and pull request. Until that pull request merges, this amendment is
Proposed; the owner's words approve the direction.

# Review standards

What blocks a merge in an independent review of this repository. This file
holds judgement rules only; every mechanical rule runs in `scripts/check.sh`.
Each rule names the incident that taught it. First round recorded
2026-11-08 ([EPG-DEC-0001](decisions/EPG-DEC-0001-reconcile-entire-and-dagger.md)
review, round 1).

- **A claim about tooling this repository delegates to must match the tooling
  outside the repository.** A decision record may say "the way-of-working
  skill keeps working unchanged" only when nothing has changed in it: changes
  to the skill's scripts — however small — are changes, and the record says
  what changed and where their PR is. Incident: round 1 of the EPG-DEC-0001
  review (2026-11-08) found a record that called the skill unchanged while
  seven of its files carried the Kimi `--auto` change.

## Code Review Results

**Scope:** `b13b872507933f2f6609a39dae35ae0f81fb2bc6` -> `20373849cd28391b5896d73430c8f3d7bc9bb929` on `guardrails/entire-dagger-coexistence` (25 files)
**Intent:** Reconcile tracked Entire hooks with local and Dagger checks while preserving operation without either tool. Close the round-1 guard, snapshot, Markdown, generated-entrypoint, decision-index, orchestration, test, and documentation defects.
**Mode:** markdown report-only

**Reviewers:** correctness, project-standards, testing, maintainability, agent-native, reliability, adversarial
- correctness -- always-on logic and intent verification
- project-standards -- root instruction files and the user-designated review standards apply
- testing -- new and changed test harnesses can create false confidence
- maintainability -- 488 non-test executable lines and duplicated guardrail sources need inspection
- agent-native -- `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are agent-facing instructions
- reliability -- failure propagation and I/O error handling are central to this change
- adversarial -- silent-pass verification mechanisms need green-while-red attacks

### Triage Groups

| Group | Findings | Context | Preferred Resolution | Why |
|-------|----------|---------|----------------------|-----|
| Dagger and local gate parity (apply queue) | #1, #6, #7 | Container inputs, invocation, and orchestration can drift while local checks stay green. | Establish one Markdown manifest and Dagger invocation contract first (#1 and #6), then add real `check.sh` integration coverage (#7). | The parity fixes need an executable integration test to prevent recurrence. |
| Fail-closed tree verification (apply queue) | #4, #5 | Snapshot coverage and Git error handling both let changes escape final verification. | Record complete filesystem entries (#4) and propagate unexpected Git failures (#5), then add independent failure-injection tests. | Both defects affect the final guard and must remain fail-closed. |

### P1 -- High

| # | File | Issue | Reviewer | Confidence |
|---|------|-------|----------|------------|
| 1 | `.dagger/modules/people-graph-ci/src/index.ts:18` | Dagger and local Markdown inputs can diverge | adversarial, testing | 100 |
| 2 | `scripts/check-decisions.mjs:46` | Decision records are not bound to unique linked IDs | correctness, adversarial, reliability, testing, maintainability | 100 |
| 3 | `scripts/hooks/pre-push:25` | Malformed pre-push input bypasses parse rejection | correctness, adversarial | 100 |
| 4 | `scripts/tree-guard.mjs:32` | Tree snapshots omit directories, dotfiles, and raw symlink bytes | adversarial, correctness, maintainability, reliability, testing | 100 |
| 5 | `scripts/tree-guard.mjs:55` | Git query failures disable index and status verification | reliability, adversarial | 100 |
| 6 | `.github/workflows/check.yml:15` | Dagger is neither enforced nor equivalent to the local gate | correctness, project-standards | 75 |
| 7 | `scripts/gates.test.sh:59` | The real `check.sh` has no integration harness | testing | 75 |

- **#1** Defect kind: divergent input definitions and vacuous-success checks.
  Affected locations: `.dagger/modules/people-graph-ci/src/index.ts:16-29` mounts only root Markdown from the repository root and omits root non-Markdown link targets; `.dagger/modules/people-graph-ci/src/index.ts:47-63` runs Markdown and link checks without asserting a nonempty tracked manifest; `scripts/check.sh:50-70` independently hard-codes local roots without reading the Dagger manifest; `ci/check-links.mjs:70-72` accepts zero files and zero targets; `AGENTS.md:59-61` requires identical Markdown populations.
  Why it matters: Dagger and local checks can pass over different or empty populations. A valid local link to a root non-Markdown file can also fail only in Dagger.
  Why review can pass: Both commands exit 0 for empty inputs. The recorded probes printed `Checked 0 Markdown files, 0 local targets, 0 broken links.` and `Linting: 0 files`. Normal fixtures do not compare the two manifests or mount a root non-Markdown target.
  Required response: Define the Markdown roots in one machine-readable manifest consumed by both entry points. Mount root non-Markdown link targets.   same checks through the local Node. Without CI, the pre-push hook is still
  the gate.

#!/bin/bash
# Lint a NUL-delimited list of Markdown files (stdin). Every listed file must
# exist on disk; an empty list is an error, not a pass. Overrides for the
# harness: MD_LINT_BIN, MD_LINT_CONFIG.
set -euo pipefail

bin=${MD_LINT_BIN:-ci/node_modules/.bin/markdownlint-cli2}
config=${MD_LINT_CONFIG:-ci/markdownlint-cli2.jsonc}

list=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lint-md.XXXXXX")
existing=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/lint-md-existing.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "$list" "$existing"' EXIT
status=0
n=0
while IFS= read -r -d '' file; do
  n=$((n + 1))
  if [ ! -f "$file" ]; then
    echo "lint-md: listed file missing on disk: $file" >&2
    status=1
    continue
  fi
  printf '%s\0' "$file" >> "$existing"
done < "$list"

if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "lint-md: $n file(s) listed; aborting before lint" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Runs the linter once with the surviving files; xargs exits nonzero when the
# linter rejects any of them.
xargs -0 "$bin" --config "$config" < "$existing"

# Agent instructions — enterprise-people-graph

Shared instructions for coding agents working in this repo (Claude Code loads
this file through [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md); Codex and Cursor read it directly).
Start at [LIONG-README](LIONG_Design_Document_Package/README.md) for
orientation, at
[LIONG-REG-001](LIONG_Design_Document_Package/LIONG-REG-001_Assumptions_Decisions_and_Open_Questions.md)
for requirement authority and open questions, and at
[the decision record index](docs/decisions/INDEX.md) for process decisions.

## Skills every agent loads

- **Writing for a person:** before writing anything a person will read, load
  the `clear-writing` skill and follow it — every reply, status update, doc,
  README, commit message, PR description, and any text the user asks to edit.
  Subagents load it too.
- **Changing the repo:** before changing anything, load the `way-of-working`
  skill and follow it. It owns the pull-request flow, the checks before every
  push, the independent review, watching open PRs, and the decision rules;
  this file points rather than restates. Where this file sets its own rule,
  this file wins; the hook wiring below is its one project-specific decision
  ([EPG-DEC-0001](docs/decisions/EPG-DEC-0001-reconcile-entire-and-dagger.md)).

## Before every push

1. **`scripts/check.sh` passes.** It runs the check tool's tests, lints the
   tracked Markdown, checks local link targets, verifies the decision-record
   index, runs the gate harness, and proves the run left the tree unchanged.
   CI ([`.github/workflows/check.yml`](.github/workflows/check.yml)) and the
   pre-push hook run the same script. `scripts/check.sh --with-dagger`
   additionally runs the container checks of the Dagger module (`.dagger`):
   Markdown structure, link targets, tool tests, and the decision-record
   check. The gate harness and the working-tree guard run locally only; a
   plain run is the same local steps without the containers.
2. **The hooks are wired.** A fresh clone runs `./scripts/bootstrap.sh` once;
   it sets `core.hooksPath` to `scripts/hooks`. Each hook chains the check
   script ahead of a verbatim copy of Entire's hook, so Entire's checkpoints
   and session-log sync keep working. With Entire absent, `commit-msg` prints
   a fallback note on stderr and the other four hooks run their non-Entire
   parts silently; each branch is asserted in `scripts/gates.test.sh`. The
   wiring shape is Decided in
   [EPG-DEC-0001](docs/decisions/EPG-DEC-0001-reconcile-entire-and-dagger.md)
   (tracked delegating hooks in `scripts/hooks`, confirmed by the owner
   2026-11-08). On a machine where Entire re-manages `.git/hooks`, that stays
   Entire's own state; this repo's hook entry point stays `scripts/hooks`.
   When the Entire CLI updates, re-diff `scripts/hooks/*` against the
   `.git/hooks` copies it installs.
3. **The independent review runs on the committed diff** before the pull
   request opens, per the `way-of-working` skill's review order. The findings
   are fixed or answered before the push.

## Working rules

- **Every change goes through a pull request.** One concern per PR. A reviewer
  merges or holds; address holds on the same branch.
- **Nothing is Decided or Approved without the owner's recorded words**, quoted
  in a [decision record](docs/decisions/INDEX.md). Decision records live in
  `docs/decisions/`; one record per decision, with its index row kept in step.
  What blocks a merge in review is in
  [REVIEW_STANDARDS.md](docs/REVIEW_STANDARDS.md).

## Entire and Dagger (EPG-DEC-0001)

- The **GitHub pull request** is the code-review and merge surface. Entire
  trails hold project-level intent across repositories: keep the trail
  description current after work, post project-level findings with
  `entire trail finding` (never as comments), and link the trail URL in the PR
  when one exists. Merging code goes through the reviewed PR, not
  `entire trail merge`.
- **Checkpoints are automatic.** The commit hooks capture the AI session; do
  not create manual checkpoints unless the owner asks.
- **Dagger** (`.dagger`, module `people-graph-ci`) runs the checks in
  containers. Its Markdown set and `scripts/check.sh`'s are one population:
  the population roots live in `scripts/md-set.sh`, and a change to the

arguments.content:
# Repo bootstrap: way-of-working, Entire, and Dagger

How to set up the standard in a new repository, whichever of the three pieces
it has. Written for the agent that does the setup, on the owner's behalf.
The owner runs every setup or destructive tool command (`entire enable`,
`entire disable`, `entire clean`, `entire login`); the agent runs everything
else. This guide's decisions trace to
[EPG-DEC-0001](../decisions/EPG-DEC-0001-reconcile-entire-and-dagger.md) in
this repository, which the owner confirmed on 2026-11-08.

## The three layers

1. **The `way-of-working` skill** — the owner's personal standard. It lives
   outside any repository and mentions neither Entire nor Dagger. It is never
   modified by a repository; a repo adapts to it, not the other way.
2. **The repository's `AGENTS.md`** — project rules, including how the tools
   slot in. Where the project rule exists, it wins over the skill.
3. **The tools** — Entire (session check-pointing, trails) and Dagger
   (container checks). Either can be absent; every layer must keep working.

## What each tool contributes, and how absence looks

| Piece | Present | Absent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entire | commit hooks capture the session as checkpoints; `entire trail` holds project-level intent across repositories; `pre-push` syncs session logs on push | the delegating hooks run their non-Entire parts (`commit-msg` prints a fallback note; the other four run silently); no checkpoints; nothing else changes |
| Dagger | `dagger check` runs the same Markdown, link, tool-test, and decision checks in containers | `scripts/check.sh` runs them with the local Node; the container gate simply is not invoked |
| CI | `.github/workflows/check.yml` runs the local gate on every push and PR | the pre-push hook is the gate |

## Setup steps

Work in this order. Copy the reference files from this repository
(`docs/agents` sits beside them) unless the target repo has its own.

1. **`AGENTS.md` and the bridge.** Write the target repo's `AGENTS.md` on the
   model of [this repo's](../../AGENTS.md): skills to load, the
   check-and-push rules with this repo's file names, the tool section, and
   pointers instead of restated rules. Point every rule at its one owner
   file. Add `CLAUDE.md` as a one-line bridge to `AGENTS.md`.
2. **The gate.** Copy `scripts/check.sh`, `scripts/md-set.sh`,
   `scripts/lint-md.sh`, `scripts/check-decisions.mjs`,
   `scripts/tree-guard.mjs`, and `scripts/gates.test.sh`. In `md-set.sh` set
   the population roots to the target repo's Markdown layout — these are the
   same roots the Dagger module mounts (step 6), one population by agreement.
3. **The hooks.** Copy `scripts/hooks/*` and `scripts/bootstrap.sh`. When
   Entire is enabled, diff each hook against the copy Entire installs in
   `.git/hooks`; every tracked hook stays a verbatim copy of Entire's, until
   the check chain in `pre-push`. Re-diff on Entire CLI updates. A git
   hook install is permitted only in the simple case of the skill's
   `guardrails.md` (no other tool owns hooks); otherwise report and ask.
4. **Decision records.** Create `docs/decisions/` with an `INDEX.md` (Record |
   Title | Status) and a first record quoting the owner's words for this
   setup, then wire the target repo's decision folder into
   `check-decisions.mjs` invocations of `check.sh` (path argument).
5. **The review standards file.** `docs/REVIEW_STANDARDS.md`, empty of rules
   except the pointer; rules land only from real findings, each with the
   incident that taught it.
6. **Dagger, if the repo has it.** Keep `dagger.toml` and the module; widen
   the module's mount to the population roots (all files under them, since
   link targets live there too), mount `scripts/` beside the tests, install
   git (Alpine: `apk add --no-cache git`) so no tool test silently skips, add
   the decisions check, and run `dagger generate` after any `src/index.ts`
   edit — the stale-source-map check fails first otherwise.
7. **CI.** Copy `.github/workflows/check.yml`; it calls `scripts/check.sh`.
   Pin action tags to refs that exist.
8. **Entire, if the repo has it.** The owner runs `entire enable` (an agent
   never runs enable, disable, clean, or auth). Verify with
   `entire agent-help`, then `entire doctor` — it must report `Git hooks: OK`
   with the tracked hooks wired.
9. **Verify, in this order** — a check that has never failed is not trusted:
   `scripts/bootstrap.sh` (sets `core.hooksPath`), `scripts/check.sh`
   (all green), break one Markdown file and expect `git hook run pre-push`
   (or a direct `sh scripts/hooks/pre-push <remote> < input`) to exit 1,
   restore, expect 0. Then commit: the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer proves the
   commit hooks work.

## The rules that bit us here (do not relearn them)

- `git checkout -- <file>` used to restore a broken test fixture also
  discards real uncommitted edits to that file. The AGENTS.md wording lost to
  it reached a review round late. Stage by name instead, or commit before
  failure-path testing.
- A shell pipeline's exit status is its last command's. `awk ... | head`
  swallowed an awk failure inside a hook. Compute with awk alone (`{ print; exit }`),
  or fail explicitly with `|| exit 1`.
- An untested check passes vacuously. Every gate added here was first made to
  fail on purpose; keep that for the next repo.
- macOS `/bin/sh` is bash in POSIX mode: no `set -o pipefail`, no `<(...)`
  process substitution. Write POSIX-compatible hooks; use `#!/bin/bash` for
  scripts that need bash features.
- `grep` patterns in assert helpers: use `grep -qF` or bracketed patterns
  silently become character classes.

## Keeping both worlds

`AGENTS.md` in the target repo states the exact same contract this repo
states: the PR is the code-review and merge surface; trails record intent and
findings, never merge code; checkpoints are automatic; the population roots
live in one file (`md-set.sh`) and a Dagger mount change is a change to them,
in the same PR. When Entire or Dagger is not installed, nothing in that
contract changes.

# Repo bootstrap: way-of-working, Entire, and Dagger

How to set up the standard in a new repository, whichever of the three pieces
it has. Written for the agent that does the setup, on the owner's behalf.
The owner runs every setup or destructive tool command (`entire enable`,
`entire disable`, `entire clean`, `entire login`); the agent runs everything
else. This guide's decisions trace to
[EPG-DEC-0001](../decisions/EPG-DEC-0001-reconcile-entire-and-dagger.md) in
this repository (source: `gh/aadehamid/enterprise-people-graph`), which the
owner confirmed on 2026-11-08.

## The three layers

1. **The `way-of-working` skill** — the owner's personal standard. It lives
   outside any repository and mentions neither Entire nor Dagger. Never
   modify it to accommodate Entire or Dagger: where review finds a genuine
   skill change, make it in `personal-agent-skills` through that
   repository's own pull request and record the changed files in the target
   repo's decision record. A repo adapts to the skill, not the other way.
2. **The repository's `AGENTS.md`** — project rules, including how the tools
   slot in. Where the project rule exists, it wins over the skill.
3. **The tools** — Entire (session check-pointing, trails) and Dagger
   (container checks). Either can be absent; every layer must keep working.

## What each tool contributes, and how absence looks

| Piece | Present | Absent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entire | commit hooks capture the session as checkpoints; `entire trail` holds project-level intent across repositories; `pre-push` syncs session logs on push | the delegating hooks run their non-Entire parts (`commit-msg` prints a fallback note; the other four run silently); no checkpoints; nothing else changes |
| Dagger | `dagger check` runs the same Markdown, link, tool-test, and decision checks in containers | `scripts/check.sh` runs them with the local Node; the container gate simply is not invoked |
| CI | `.github/workflows/check.yml` runs the local gate on every push and PR | the pre-push hook is the gate |

## Setup steps

Work in this order. Copy from this repository — each name below exists in the
branch that carries this file.

1. **`AGENTS.md` and the bridge.** Write the target repo's `AGENTS.md` on the
   model of [this repo's](../../AGENTS.md): skills to load, the
   check-and-push rules with the target's file names, the tool section, and
   pointers instead of restated rules. Point every rule at its one owner
   file. Add `CLAUDE.md` as a one-line bridge to `AGENTS.md`.
2. **The `.gitignore` rules first.** Add `**/node_modules/` (any other tool
   state folders the tools write into `.gitignore` too), and, when Dagger is
   present, keep `dagger.lock` tracked and copied from this repo's.
3. **The gate and its tools.** Copy `scripts/check.sh`, `scripts/md-set.sh`,
   `scripts/lint-md.sh`, `scripts/check-decisions.mjs`,
   `scripts/tree-guard.mjs`, and `scripts/gates.test.sh` — plus the whole
   tracked `ci/` directory the gate depends on: `ci/package.json`,
   `ci/package-lock.json`, `ci/markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`, `ci/check-links.mjs`,
   `ci/check-links.test.mjs`, `ci/check-decisions.test.mjs`,
   `ci/tree-guard.test.mjs` (never `ci/node_modules`). In `scripts/md-set.sh`
   set the population roots to the target repo's Markdown layout — these are
   the same roots the Dagger module mounts (step 7), one population by
   agreement.
4. **Decision records.** Create the target's decision folder (default
   `docs/decisions/`) with an `INDEX.md` (Record | Title | Status) and a
   first record quoting the owner's words for this setup, then set the
   target's decision folder and record prefix in three places so local and
   container checks see one population: the environment or `DECISIONS_DIR` /
   `DECISION_PREFIX` lines in `scripts/check.sh`, the
   `check-decisions.mjs` arguments in the Dagger module (`src/index.ts`),
   and the folder in the module's mount. The defaults in this repo are
   `docs/decisions` and the record prefix `EPG-DEC`.
5. **The review standards file.** `docs/REVIEW_STANDARDS.md`, holding only
   the pointer to the instruction file it judges — the target's own
   `AGENTS.md` requirements — and empty of rules until a reviewer actually
   makes a finding; each rule names the incident that taught it.
6. **The hooks.** Copy `scripts/hooks/*` and `scripts/bootstrap.sh`. A git
   hook install is permitted only in the simple case of the skill's
   `guardrails.md` (default `hooksPath`, no other tool owns hooks, one
   worktree); otherwise report and ask. When Entire is enabled (step 8),
   diff each hook against the copy Entire installs in `.git/hooks`; every
   tracked hook stays a verbatim copy of Entire's, until the check chain in
   `pre-push`. Re-diff on Entire CLI updates.
7. **Dagger, if the repo has it.** Keep `dagger.toml` and the module, and
   copy `dagger.lock`. Set the decision folder in the `decisions` check
   (step 4) and include the target's decision folder in the mount. Widen the
   module's mount to the population roots (all files under them, since link
   targets live there too), keep the `scripts/` and `.github/**` mounts that
   the tool tests and link targets need, install git (`apk add --no-cache
   git` on Alpine) so no tool test silently skips, and run `dagger generate`
   after any `src/index.ts` edit — the stale-source-map check fails first
   otherwise. Run `dagger check` and expect one passing check per check
   defined; then break one input and expect the container check to fail
   before restoring it. `scripts/check.sh --with-dagger` runs the same
   container checks locally, inside the tree guard's snapshot.
8. **CI.** Copy `.github/workflows/check.yml`; it calls `scripts/check.sh`.
   Pin action tags to refs that exist.
9. **Entire, if the repo has it.** The owner runs `entire enable` (an agent
   never runs enable, disable, clean, or auth). Then, in order: diff the
   hooks per step 6, run `scripts/bootstrap.sh`, confirm `git config
   core.hooksPath` prints `scripts/hooks`, and run `entire doctor` — it must
   report `Git hooks: OK` with the tracked hooks wired.
10. **Verify, in this order** — a check that has never failed is not trusted.
    The target's Markdown must be staged (`git add -- <named setup files>`)
    and `HEAD` must exist before the full gate: run `scripts/bootstrap.sh`
    (if not already), make the initial commit of the setup files, and only
    then run `scripts/check.sh` (all green). For the failure path, break one
    tracked Markdown file, pipe a valid four-field, nondeletion ref record
    (`refs/heads/main <HEAD sha> refs/heads/test 0000…0`, the local sha of
    the current commit) into `sh scripts/hooks/pre-push origin`, and require
    exit 1 with the injected diagnostic (an **empty stdin does not run the
    checks** — that is the hook's own contract, tested in
    `scripts/gates.test.sh`); restore the file with `git restore --worktree
    -- <file>` and repeat the same input, expecting exit 0. For the final
    commit: with Entire present and verified, the commit carries the
    `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer; with Entire absent, require a successful
    commit and the `commit-msg` fallback note instead — the trailer cannot
    exist there.

## The rules that bit us here (do not relearn them)

- `git checkout -- <file>` used to restore a broken test fixture also
  discards real uncommitted edits to that file. The AGENTS.md wording lost to
  it reached a review round late. Stage by name instead, or commit before
  failure-path testing.
- A shell pipeline's exit status is its last command's. `awk ... | head`
  swallowed an awk failure inside a hook. Compute with awk alone (`{ print; exit }`),
  or fail explicitly with `|| exit 1`.
- An untested check passes vacuously. Every gate added here was first made to
  fail on purpose; keep that for the next repo.
- macOS `/bin/sh` is bash in POSIX mode: no `set -o pipefail`, no `<(...)`
  process substitution. Write POSIX-compatible hooks; use `#!/bin/bash` for
  scripts that need bash features.
- `grep` patterns in assert helpers: use `grep -qF` or bracketed patterns
  silently become character classes.

## Keeping both worlds

`AGENTS.md` in the target repo states the exact same contract this repo
states: the PR is the code-review and merge surface; trails record intent and
findings, never merge code; checkpoints are automatic; the population roots
live in one file (`md-set.sh`) and a Dagger mount change is a change to them,
in the same PR. When Entire or Dagger is not installed, nothing in that
contract changes.
